config.properties.gitWorkflowHelper.targ: Optional target branches list, supports adding more branches. E.g.: `["uat", "pre", "prod"]`

Optional target branches list, supports adding more branches

Example: `["uat", "pre", "prod"]`

You can add, remove, and edit items directly in the settings page
config.properties.gitWorkflowHelper.bran: Branch prefix configuration for creating standardized branch names. E.g.: `["feature", "bugfix", "hotfix"]`

Branch prefix configuration for creating standardized branch names

Example: `["feature", "bugfix", "hotfix"]`

You can add, remove, and edit items directly in the settings page
config.properties.gitWorkflowHelper.cust: Custom Git username (leave empty to use Git config), used for branch naming
config.properties.gitWorkflowHelper.bran: Custom branch name template. Only takes effect when "Branch Naming Template Preset" is set to "Custom Template". Supported placeholders: {prefix}, {date}, {description}, {username}
Branch naming template preset, can be quickly selected in settings
config.properties.gitWorkflowHelper.auto: Automatically checkout to the new branch after creation
config.properties.gitWorkflowHelper.maxC: Maximum number of conflicting files to open in batch when merging (1-20)
config.properties.gitWorkflowHelper.skip: Whether to always skip Git hooks (e.g. pre-commit) when rolling back using revert (--no-verify)
config.properties.gitWorkflowHelper.maxC: Maximum number of commits displayed in the list during batch cherry-pick (10-200)
config.properties.gitWorkflowHelper.cher: Use -x to record the origin in the commit message during batch cherry-pick
Advanced: Application order of merge/author/time filters. Keywords can be searched in the top bar of the commit list, no configuration needed
config.properties.gitWorkflowHelper.merg: git reset --hard to before merge (only available if merge is the latest commit, does not create revert commit)
git revert -m 1 to create reverse commit (retains history, suitable if there are subsequent commits or pushed)
Ask to choose reset or revert before each rollback
Strategy used when rolling back a merge into the current branch (default reset, not revert)
config.properties.gitWorkflowHelper.comm: Custom commit message templates. Can be a string (e.g. "ci: {description}") or an object (id, name, description, template)

Custom commit message templates, appearing in "Formatted Commit" alongside built-in Conventional Commits templates.

- String: `"ci: {description}"`
- Object: `{ "id": "ci", "name": "CI", "template": "ci: {description}" }`

Placeholders: `{description}`, `{scope}`, `{ticket}`, `{username}`
config.properties.gitWorkflowHelper.defa: Default highlighted template id during formatted commit (built-in like feat, fix; or custom template id)
extension.description: Git workflow tool: standardize branching, guide merges, formatted commits (Conventional Commits), resolve conflicts, batch cherry-pick, merge rollback and force-with-lease.
